section: Regulation and ethics of biotechnology - GEAC, biosafety, bioethics, biopiracy, IPR and the ethical/social/legal debate
subsections: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans
IPR in biotech - Patents Act, PPVFR Act 2001, Novartis and PepsiCo cases
Seed technologies in controversy - GURT / terminator seeds

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the apex statutory body regulating genetically modified organisms in India?
o: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
accepted.x: The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC) is the apex statutory body regulating GMOs in India. FSSAI, CPCB and ICAR are not the apex GMO regulator.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the correct regulatory authority from closely related bodies.
accepted.sec: GEAC - ministry, Act, chair, role

accepted.s: The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee is chaired by:
o: The Special or Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
The Chairperson of the Central Pollution Control Board
The Director-General of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research
accepted.x: GEAC is chaired by a Special or Additional Secretary of MoEFCC. A senior officer from the Department of Biotechnology serves as co-chair.
accepted.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to identify the correct chairing authority.
accepted.sec: GEAC - ministry, Act, chair, role

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee?
o: Approving field trials of genetically modified crops
Approving commercial release and cultivation of GM organisms
Approving large-scale use of hazardous microorganisms and recombinants
Fixing the maximum retail price of all commercial seeds
accepted.x: GEAC deals with field trials, environmental release, commercial cultivation and large-scale use of hazardous microorganisms and recombinants. Fixing the maximum retail price of all commercial seeds is not its function.
accepted.tq: Find the one unrelated function among powers of the same regulatory body.
accepted.sec: GEAC - ministry, Act, chair, role

accepted.s: The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee was renamed the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee in:
accepted.x: The committee was renamed from Genetic Engineering Approval Committee to Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee in 2010.
accepted.tq: Use the exact year to distinguish a renamed institution from nearby biotechnology events.
accepted.sec: GEAC - ministry, Act, chair, role

accepted.s: Which of the following is regarded as the primary environmental concern associated with genetically modified crops?
o: Cross-pollination and gene flow to non-GM crops
Reduction in soil mineral content in every cultivated field
Increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide from all crops
accepted.x: The primary environmental concern is cross-pollination or gene flow from GM crops to non-GM crops. The other effects are not identified as the primary concern.
accepted.tq: Select the precise environmental impact rather than a general ecological claim.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s:
Consider the following possible risks of genetically modified crops:
1. Development of insect resistance
2. Harm to non-target organisms
3. Weediness in wild relatives
4. Genetic homogenisation
Which of the above are recognised environmental concerns?
accepted.x: Insect resistance, harm to non-target organisms, weediness in wild relatives and genetic homogenisation are all recognised environmental concerns associated with GM crops.
accepted.tq: Test whether all items in a same-theme risk list are correctly included.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents health-related concerns associated with genetically modified crops?
o: Ozone depletion, acid rain and eutrophication
Noise pollution, thermal pollution and vibration
accepted.x: The health-related concerns identified are toxicity, allergenicity and antibiotic resistance. The other combinations describe unrelated environmental problems.
accepted.tq: Group the effects by subject area and reject risks belonging to other environmental topics.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Introduction of Bt cotton
B. PIL against GM crops in the Supreme Court
C. Moratorium on Bt brinjal
D. GEAC clearance of trials of 11 crops and 21 varieties
accepted.x: Bt cotton was introduced in 2002, the PIL was filed in 2006, the Bt brinjal moratorium was imposed in 2010, and GEAC cleared trials in 2014.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last events, then place the intervening years in sequence.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s: The 2010 decision relating to Bt brinjal included which of the following additional measures?
o: A requirement that all GM seeds be branded by the State
A transfer of field-trial approval exclusively to FSSAI
A mandatory State no-objection certificate for field trials
A permanent ban on every GM crop in India
accepted.x: In 2010, a State NOC was made mandatory for field trials. The decision was not a permanent ban on every GM crop or a transfer of approval to FSSAI.
accepted.tq: Separate the specific administrative condition from exaggerated consequences.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s: Which report recommended ending all genetically modified crop field trials?
o: The report of the Central Pollution Control Board
The 37th Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Agriculture
The annual report of the National Biodiversity Authority
The report of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
accepted.x: The 37th Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Agriculture in 2012 recommended ending all GM field trials.
accepted.tq: Identify the report by matching the recommendation with the correct parliamentary body.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court-appointed Technical Expert Committee:
1. It recommended a 10-year moratorium on GM field trials.
2. Its recommendation amounted to a final Supreme Court verdict.
3. GM trials were halted during the relevant period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Technical Expert Committee recommended a 10-year moratorium and trials were halted. The recommendation was not itself a final Supreme Court verdict.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an expert recommendation from a judicial verdict.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the change in field-trial policy in 2014?
o: Trials were permanently prohibited by the Supreme Court.
The State NOC requirement was abolished for all field trials.
Veerappa Moily resumed trials and GEAC cleared trials of 11 crops in March and 21 varieties in July.
Jairam Ramesh imposed a new moratorium on all crops.
accepted.x: In 2014, Veerappa Moily resumed trials; GEAC cleared trials of 11 crops in March and 21 varieties in July. The moratorium was not made permanent and the State NOC requirement was not stated to have been abolished.
accepted.tq: Use the dates and numerical figures to distinguish resumption from suspension.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding field trials of GM crops is correct?
o: State-level approval is unnecessary when GEAC grants approval.
Field trials require the State's no-objection certificate, and several States have refused such permission.
Only the Department of Biotechnology can grant State-level permission.
State governments have no role in field trials.
accepted.x: Field trials require the State's NOC, and several States have refused to provide it. This creates an important element of State-level control.
accepted.tq: Apply the federal administrative condition to a field-trial scenario.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations correctly explains delays in approval of genetically modified products in India?
o: Overlapping mandates of DBT, GEAC, CDSCO, FSSAI and NBA, along with the absence of a biosafety liability law
Exclusive control of approval by ICAR and the presence of a comprehensive liability law
Absence of all environmental regulation and exclusive control by State governments
Only the high cost of imported seeds
accepted.x: Overlapping mandates among DBT, GEAC, CDSCO, FSSAI and NBA, together with the absence of a biosafety liability law, contribute to delays. Approval may take 7–10 years in India compared with 3–5 years globally.
accepted.tq: Combine the institutional and legal causes instead of selecting a single-factor explanation.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s: Approval of which GM crop for environmental release was cleared by GEAC in 2022?
accepted.x: GEAC cleared the environmental release of DMH-11 mustard in 2022. Bt cotton, Bt brinjal and FL-2027 potato relate to different events in the GM debate.
accepted.tq: Match the crop with the specific year and regulatory action.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s: The July 2024 split verdict concerning GM mustard involved which additional direction by both judges?
o: To transfer all approvals to State governments
To frame a national policy on GM crops
To prohibit all agricultural field trials for ten years
accepted.x: In July 2024, both judges in the split verdict on GM mustard directed the Centre to frame a national GM crop policy.
accepted.tq: Focus on the common direction in a split verdict rather than the divided outcome.
accepted.sec: GM debate - environmental concerns, field trials, TEC report, state bans

accepted.s: Which provision of the Patents Act excludes plants, animals, seeds and essentially biological processes from patentability while permitting patenting of microbial processes?
accepted.x: Section 3(j) excludes plants, animals, seeds and essentially biological processes from patentability, while microbial processes can be patented.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely numbered statutory provisions by their subject matter.
accepted.sec: IPR in biotech - Patents Act, PPVFR Act 2001, Novartis and PepsiCo cases

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Section 3(d) of the Patents Act:
1. It bars a patent for a new form of a known substance unless enhanced efficacy is shown.
2. It is intended to prevent evergreening.
3. It makes all microbial processes non-patentable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Section 3(d) requires enhanced efficacy for a new form of a known substance and acts against evergreening. It does not make all microbial processes non-patentable.
accepted.tq: Separate the purpose of Section 3(d) from the distinct subject matter of Section 3(j).
accepted.sec: IPR in biotech - Patents Act, PPVFR Act 2001, Novartis and PepsiCo cases

accepted.s: The Supreme Court decision in Novartis v. Union of India (2013) upheld rejection of the patent for Glivec under:
accepted.x: In Novartis v. Union of India, the Supreme Court upheld rejection of the Glivec (imatinib) patent under Section 3(d) of the Patents Act.
accepted.tq: Match the landmark case with the correct statutory provision and subject.
accepted.sec: IPR in biotech - Patents Act, PPVFR Act 2001, Novartis and PepsiCo cases

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the principal subject of protection under the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001?
accepted.x: The PPVFR Act, 2001 protects plant varieties and farmers' rights. It is distinct from provisions governing pharmaceutical patents or biosafety approval.
accepted.tq: Identify the scope of a specialised intellectual-property law.
accepted.sec: IPR in biotech - Patents Act, PPVFR Act 2001, Novartis and PepsiCo cases

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the PepsiCo potato case:
1. PepsiCo sued Gujarat farmers over the FL-2027 (FC5) potato variety.
2. The suits were subsequently withdrawn.
3. The PPVFR Authority revoked the registration of the variety in 2021.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: PepsiCo sued Gujarat farmers over its FL-2027 (FC5) variety, later withdrew the suits, and the PPVFR Authority revoked the registration in 2021.
accepted.tq: Check all stages of a legal case—claim, withdrawal and subsequent regulatory action.
accepted.sec: IPR in biotech - Patents Act, PPVFR Act 2001, Novartis and PepsiCo cases

accepted.s: Under the farmers' rights recognised in the relevant legal framework, farmers may save, use, sow, resow, exchange, share and sell farm produce including seed, but may not:
o: Save seed from their own produce
accepted.x: Farmers may save, use, sow, resow, exchange, share and sell farm produce including seed, but they may not sell branded seed.
accepted.tq: Apply the legal distinction between ordinary farm produce and branded seed.
accepted.sec: IPR in biotech - Patents Act, PPVFR Act 2001, Novartis and PepsiCo cases

accepted.s: GURT is an acronym for:
accepted.x: GURT stands for Genetic Use Restriction Technology. One controversial form is popularly known as the terminator seed technology.
accepted.tq: Expand the exact acronym instead of selecting a look-alike biotechnology term.
accepted.sec: Seed technologies in controversy - GURT / terminator seeds

accepted.s: What is the principal feature of terminator seeds?
o: They produce sterile seeds, requiring farmers to buy fresh seed each season.
They can be resown indefinitely without any new purchase.
They permanently increase the fertility of all neighbouring crops.
They prevent all insect resistance in cultivated crops.
accepted.x: Terminator seeds produce sterile seeds, so farmers must buy fresh seed each season. This creates concerns about dependency on seed companies and loss of seed-saving practices.
accepted.tq: Infer the economic consequence from the biological feature of the technology.
accepted.sec: Seed technologies in controversy - GURT / terminator seeds

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the PPVFR Act and GURT is correct?
o: The Act mandates registration of all varieties carrying GURT.
The Act bars registration of varieties carrying GURT.
The Act has no provision concerning GURT.
The Act permits registration only when farmers cannot save seed.
accepted.x: The PPVFR Act bars registration of varieties carrying Genetic Use Restriction Technology. This reflects concerns over seed dependency and loss of farmers' seed-saving rights.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversed legal relationship between a statute and a controversial technology.
accepted.sec: Seed technologies in controversy - GURT / terminator seeds

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an objection raised by farmers against GURT or terminator seeds?
o: Guaranteed improvement in farmers' autonomy over seed supply
Higher recurring costs of purchasing seed
accepted.x: Farmers' objections include dependency on companies, recurring costs and loss of seed-saving. Guaranteed improvement in seed autonomy is contrary to these objections.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of the stated social and economic concerns.
accepted.sec: Seed technologies in controversy - GURT / terminator seeds
